name: IBM
overview: IBM is a technology company that works in areas such as hybrid cloud, AI, mainframe, consulting and quantum. In India it hires freshers mainly as Associate System Engineers and entry-level software engineers through campus and off-campus drives. IBM says its hiring steps vary by location and region.
variation_note: IBM says the process varies by role, location and region; candidate reports from 2021 to 2026 show different mixes of coding, English, games, group discussion and interview rounds, so check what your college drive announces.

roles.title: Associate System Engineer (ASE)
roles.description: Entry-level role to design, code, test, debug and maintain software applications, mainly for IBM Consulting projects.

eligibility.text: 65% or 6.5 CGPA in graduation; 2026 passouts; B.E/B.Tech, M.E/M.Tech, BCA/MCA, B.Sc/M.Sc
6.0 CGPA minimum, CS/IT/semi-IT streams, no active backlogs (2025 campus drive report)
Required education: Bachelor's degree (IBM India job posting)

compensation.text: 4.5 LPA + 25,000 one-time settling allowance (as reported, 2025 campus drive)

roles.title: Software Engineer (entry level)
roles.description: Entry-level developer role listed by IBM India for freshers; same online assessment style as ASE according to third-party pages.

eligibility.text: Same eligibility table as ASE on PrepInsta (60% in 10th/12th, 65% or 6.5 CGPA in graduation, no active backlog)

stages.name: Application and screening
stages.what: You apply online (or through your college drive) and IBMers review your application, skills and experience.

format.text: Application, screening, online assessment, interview, decision

study: Resume with clear projects and skills
tips: Apply to one job ID at a time; track status in the IBM candidate portal
Keep government ID with exact name and date of birth ready
stages.before_next: Practise easy and medium coding problems on HackerRank-style editors.
stages.label: Official

stages.name: Online coding assessment
stages.what: Coding problems (and sometimes MCQs) on HackerRank. Some drives add a second, harder coding round later.

format.text: Set of multiple-choice questions or coding challenges depending on the role
2 coding questions / 55 min (with a 10-question English test, 65 min total)
2 coding questions, approx. 60 min, plus 5 to 6 MCQs on DBMS, OS, OOP, programming
HackerRank, MCQ + coding (DSA, aptitude, OOP), about 60 to 90 min; later an in-person round with 1 array/string problem in about 30 min (2025 campus drive)
HackerRank, 2 coding questions (easy + medium); a later Advanced Coding round on HackerRank had much tougher questions (2026 batch on-campus)
IBM CodeKnack: 1 coding question in 30 min on HackerRank with 7 test cases (2023)
1 coding question in 30 min; about 82 of 330 applicants shortlisted (older on-campus report)

tips: Read the input format carefully and handle invalid inputs even if not stated
Run your code on edge cases before submitting
Practise in the HackerRank editor so the setup feels normal
stages.before_next: Be able to solve 2 easy-medium problems in under 55 minutes.
stages.label: Candidate-reported

stages.name: English language and communication assessment
stages.what: A timed English test (grammar, spelling, vocabulary). Some drives use a spoken test or typed answers to behavioural questions, and IBM may also use a video assessment.

format.text: English language assessment: text-based multiple-choice questions; a video assessment (webcam answers to interview questions) may also be used
10 questions / 10 min: voice, fill in the blanks, error spotting, spelling, synonyms, antonyms
15 min MCQ with negative marking: spelling, grammar errors, word meaning
10 min, 3 sections, negative marking; use the '?' option when unsure
AI-proctored spoken English test, then in-person typed answers to 5 behavioural questions with a 5-minute timer each (2025 campus drive)

tips: There can be negative marking, so skip when unsure
For typed answers use short STAR stories: situation, task, action, result
stages.before_next: Prepare 4 or 5 short STAR stories from your projects and teamwork.
stages.label: Candidate-reported

stages.name: Cognitive ability games (older pattern)
stages.what: Short puzzle games on numbers, logic and spelling. Older reports had this round; PrepInsta's 2026 page says it is not asked anymore.

format.text: 5 games in 30 min (older on-campus report)
6 logical and mathematical games in 30 min (older report)
Six mini-games (e.g. Shortcuts, Gridlock, Resemble, Tally Up, Numbubbles, Proof It); marked NOT ASKED ANYMORE for the 2026 batch

tips: Do not spend long preparing unless your drive mentions games
stages.before_next: Check your drive's email to see if games are included.
stages.label: Candidate-reported

stages.name: Group discussion
stages.what: Some campus drives hold a group discussion on a general topic before the interview.

format.text: Round 2: group discussion on abstract topics, social issues or current affairs
Group discussion after the English test; topic was 'Cinema vs OTT Platforms' (2023)

tips: Speak early with one clear point
Let others finish and build on their points
Summarise at the end if you get the chance
stages.before_next: Revise your projects and core CS for the interview.
stages.label: Candidate-reported

stages.name: Technical + HR interview
stages.what: One interview that covers your projects, programming basics, DBMS/SQL and HR questions.

format.text: Interview by phone, video or in person, or an assessment centre (group exercise + interview)
Final interview about 30 min (older report)
In-person Technical + HR interview; final 66 selected (2025 campus drive)

tips: Know what you wrote on your resume
Be ready for 'What do you know about IBM?' and relocation questions
stages.before_next: Keep ID and marksheets ready; IBM may ask for background verification documents.
stages.label: Candidate-reported

questions.subject: Coding
questions.question: Input is two numbers: one hexadecimal and one decimal. Print EQUAL if they have the same value, else NOT EQUAL. Handle invalid numbers.
questions.answer: Convert with int(h,16) and int(d) and compare; catch ValueError for invalid input. '1A' and '26' gives EQUAL, 'FF' and '254' gives NOT EQUAL.
questions.label: Candidate-reported

questions.subject: Coding
questions.question: Find all numbers in a given string and print them; if a number ends with three zeros, replace them with one zero (1000 becomes 10).
questions.answer: Use re.findall(r'\d+', s); for each number ending in '000', drop those three zeros and add one '0'. 'abc1000def25' gives 10 and 25.
questions.label: Candidate-reported

questions.subject: Coding
questions.question: Valid password checker: check whether a password is valid (for example at least 8 characters with an uppercase letter, a lowercase letter, a digit and a special character).
questions.answer: Check length, then use any() with isupper, islower, isdigit and a non-alphanumeric test. 'Nmit@2024' is valid, 'password1' is not.
questions.label: Candidate-reported

questions.subject: Coding
questions.question: Write a program to find the LCM of two numbers.
questions.label: Candidate-reported

questions.subject: Coding
questions.question: Write the Fibonacci series recursively and iteratively, and give the time complexity of each.
questions.answer: Plain recursion is O(2^n) because it repeats work; the loop version is O(n) time and O(1) space.
questions.label: Candidate-reported

questions.subject: DBMS
questions.question: What is a foreign key?
questions.answer: A column in one table that refers to the primary key of another table, so related rows stay consistent.
questions.label: Candidate-reported

questions.subject: Other
questions.question: Linked list vs array: what is the difference?
questions.answer: Arrays are contiguous with O(1) index access but costly inserts; linked lists use nodes with pointers, O(1) insert at a known node but O(n) access.
questions.label: Candidate-reported

questions.subject: Logical
questions.question: Convert the word 'warm' to 'cold' by changing one letter at a time, with every step a real word, in 4 changes.
questions.answer: warm, ward, card, cord, cold. Each step changes one letter and is a real word.
questions.label: Candidate-reported

questions.subject: Other
questions.question: Is String mutable? Explain mutable vs immutable types.
questions.answer: Mutable objects can change in place (Python list, dict); immutable ones cannot (Python str, tuple; Java String). 'Changing' a string creates a new object.
questions.label: Candidate-reported

questions.subject: SQL
questions.question: What are the types of SQL joins and how do they differ?
questions.answer: INNER (matching rows only), LEFT (all left rows + matches), RIGHT (all right rows + matches), FULL OUTER (all rows from both), CROSS (every pair), SELF (table joined with itself).
questions.label: Candidate-reported

questions.subject: Other
questions.question: What are List, Tuple and Dictionary in Python?
questions.answer: List: ordered and mutable. Tuple: ordered and immutable. Dictionary: key-value pairs with fast lookup by key.
questions.label: Candidate-reported

questions.subject: HR
questions.question: Tell me about a time when a team member was not cooperating on a project. What did you do?
questions.answer: Use STAR: the situation, your task, what you did (talked privately, split work clearly, set check-ins), and the result.
questions.label: Candidate-reported

questions.subject: Verbal
questions.question: Choose the correct passive form: 'The team completed the project.'
options: The project completed by the team.
The project was completed by the team.
The project is completed by the team.
The project had completed by the team.
questions.answer: 'The project was completed by the team.' Simple past active becomes was/were + past participle.
questions.label: AI practice
